audit: GSE research-to-code reconciliation -- gaps and contradictions

gaps.title: Oct-18 published picks are clamped into a fixed window, not the engine's output
gaps.claim_tested: The live board that shipped Week 6 sides/totals/MLs/props/SGPs on 2026-10-18 shows the GSE engine's published confidence, edge score and pick grade.
evidence: scripts/publish_late_sun_mon_live_free.py:498  true_prob = max(0.6020, min(0.6160, sig_attr["trueProb"]))
scripts/publish_late_sun_mon_live_free.py:502  edge_score = min(71.2, max(68.4, sig_attr["edgeScore"]))
scripts/publish_late_sun_mon_live_free.py:503  confidence = max(66, min(69, sig_attr["confidence"]))
scripts/publish_late_sun_mon_live_free.py:504  tier = "FREE"
scripts/publish_late_sun_mon_live_free.py:505  pick_grade = "STRONG_PLAY"   # hardcoded, no threshold
scripts/sync_week6_db.py:257-261,758-761  # the EARLIER writer derives these from raw_edge (no clamp)
apps/web/lib/board/state.ts:495, apps/web/lib/board/load-gate-slate.ts:580, apps/web/lib/board/passes.ts:154  # public board reads isPublished:true rows
gaps.impact: Published confidence, edgeScore and pickGrade are not engine outputs. The grade is hardcoded to the strongest value for every pick regardless of the model's own view. Any downstream CLV, settlement, calibration or ledger analysis on these rows measures the clamp, not the model.
gaps.recommended_action: Remove all four clamps; publish sig_attr values unmodified. Add a CI assertion that published pickGrade is derived, never literal.

gaps.claim_tested: The walk-forward gate (walk-forward-gate.json) protects emission of picks.
evidence: packages/ingestion-pipeline/walk-forward-gate.json  ->  "passed": false, "crps": null, "gaussian_close_crps": 7.154021 (gate requires CRPS <= 7.099)
packages/ingestion-pipeline/src/walk-forward-emission-gate.ts:19-31  readEmissionGate() -> emissionBlocked(), fail-closed on missing file
packages/ingestion-pipeline/src/generate-signal-slate.ts:265  if (emissionBlocked(opts.emissionGate)) -> returns 0 picks, note 'emission gate closed: 0 picks, 0 parlays, 0 DFS'

gaps.impact: The TS board-fill slate emits nothing because its gate is closed; the content that actually shipped bypassed the gate entirely. The gate is doing no safety work.
gaps.recommended_action: Decide the gate's real scope. Either (a) make every publish path consult readEmissionGate(), or (b) delete the gate from the TS path and re-home it where it has meaning. Also resolve the outstanding CRPS<=7.099 criterion.

gaps.claim_tested: The Reasoning Engine ingests thousands of literature records continuously.

gaps.impact: On Vercel the corpus evaluator loads 0 items (returns [] rather than throwing) and the mind corpus throws unless a repo-relative path happens to resolve. Either way the reasoning corpus is absent in production while present in local dev -- the exact class of drift this audit is about.
gaps.recommended_action: Resolve both corpora via an explicit env var (GSE_CORPUS_DIR / GSE_MIND_CORPUS) with a repo-relative fallback, bundle the corpus in the build, or skip the evaluation explicitly when unavailable instead of silently evaluating 0 items.

packages/prediction-engine/src/calibration-apply.ts:73  buildCalibrator -- imported only by apps/web/lib/calibration/calibration-audit-harness.ts:26 (an audit harness, not the scoring path)

gaps.impact: 21 of 22 packages/prediction-engine/src/calibration/* modules, plus all 5 continual/* modules, plus the online-beta and calibration-ladder recalibration paths, have zero production consumers. The only calibration effect in production is a withhold (packages/prediction-engine/src/calibration/pathwise-defect.ts:201 calibrationHistoryWithholds, imported at scoring.ts:14) which can block a pick but never adjust one. The system cannot currently learn from its own results.
gaps.recommended_action: Pick the one recalibration path to promote (online-beta-recalibration is the natural candidate -- it is designed for exactly this), wire it behind the existing promotion gates, and land the pre-registration it requires. Until then, stop describing the engine as self-improving.

gaps.impact: Published raw edge for most Week 6 picks was computed against 0.5000 rather than a de-vigged book consensus. With trueProb clamped to [0.6020,0.6160], the published raw edge is 0.1020-0.1160 by construction, not by model.

gaps.title: The reasoning surfaces are architecturally forbidden from ever being a pick
gaps.claim_tested: The Reasoning Engine produces picks with edges that get published.
evidence: packages/prediction-engine/src/reasoning/aggregation-trace.ts:229  publishablePick: false
packages/ingestion-pipeline/src/reasoning-trace.ts:139  'A reasoning trace is not a pick. publishablePick is false. beatsBookClaim is false.'
packages/ingestion-pipeline/src/reasoning-trace.ts:202  publishablePick: false

packages/ingestion-pipeline/src/gse-score-bridge.ts:297  publishablePick: false
packages/prediction-engine/src/reasoning/situational-engine.ts:169  divergenceIsEdge: false
gaps.impact: The type system encodes 'reasoning never becomes a pick' as a literal false in five places. This was the correct posture while predictions were unpublished. Under the current model it means the Reasoning Engine is structurally barred from ever being the thing that is published -- the opposite of the stated product direction.
gaps.recommended_action: This is a doctrine decision, not a patch. Either the reasoning layer stays a non-pick advisory layer (and the product statement should say the engine publishes market-anchored picks with reasoning as explanation), or the type is changed to allow a reasoning-derived pick through a promotion gate.

gaps.title: walk-forward-gate.json self-documents an unimplemented research path
gaps.claim_tested: The walk-forward gate evaluates the Laplace CRPS.

gaps.title: The repo's own 'every paper is wired' index is a bucket-tagging artifact, not code
gaps.claim_tested: WIRE-IN-PLAN.md claims every one of the 1,251 tracker papers is mapped into an engine bucket and is 'wired to the engine'.

docs/arxiv-program/research/2026-09-21/arxiv-program/index/WIRE-IN-PLAN.md:32  print('WIRE-IN OK: 1251/1251, every paper in >=1 bucket')
MEASURED: 1,511 arxiv-deep ledgers, 1,442 unique arXiv IDs; only 291 IDs have an implementing module (20%)
MEASURED: 306 arXiv-derived modules in packages/prediction-engine/src; 7 are called by another engine module, 47 are barrel-only, 251 are imported by nothing
MEASURED: 306/306 of those modules DO have a sibling .test.ts -- the test is the only thing exercising them
gaps.impact: 'Wired' in this repo's index means 'a string was written into corpus-index.jsonl', not 'code exists and is called'. A reader of WIRE-IN-PLAN.md would conclude 100% of the research corpus is in the engine. Measured code coverage is 20%. The gap between the two numbers is the single largest misstatement in the repository.
gaps.recommended_action: Rewrite WIRE-IN-PLAN.md to state the measured number and define 'wired' as 'imported by a production path', not 'tagged in a bucket'. Add a CI check that re-derives the count from the import graph so the doc cannot drift again.

gaps.recommended_action: Decide per gate: wire it, or move it to an explicit 'research' directory so the file tree stops implying coverage. A gate that cannot block should not be counted as a gate.

gaps.title: The no-publish doctrine is enforced by a CI guardrail, a default-ON kill switch, a runtime throw, and TypeScript literal types
gaps.claim_tested: The old restriction against publishing predictions is prose and has been removed as doctrine.
evidence: scripts/guardrails/draft-only.mjs:5-11  'Fails CI if any API / page / lib / worker file performs a publish-side write' -- scans 3,716 files, exits 0 today
scripts/guardrails/draft-only.mjs:225-227  blocks publishedAt: new Date(, status: 'PUBLISHED', and non-null publishedAt in any data block
.github/workflows/ci.yml:237-252  the 'Draft-only (no auto-publish)' job, whose own comment says 'outside the explicit (and currently non-existent) publish boundary'
workers/content-publishing/src/index.ts:15  INTERNAL_CALIBRATION_ONLY = process.env['INTERNAL_CALIBRATION_ONLY'] !== 'false' -- DEFAULT ON, so every request returns REFUSED (:32-38)
apps/web/lib/content-engine/persist-draft.ts:60-65  throw new Error('...refusing to persist a record with publishedAt set')
apps/web/lib/jarvis/agent-council.ts:88,90  readonly externalActions: 'NONE'; readonly externalActionsAllowed: false; -- LITERAL TYPES, so agent publishing is a COMPILE ERROR
apps/web/lib/agents/agent-capabilities.ts:8  FORBIDDEN_EXTERNAL_ACTIONS includes PUBLISH, SEND_EXTERNAL, ENABLE_PUBLIC_PICKS -- publish is FORBIDDEN, not GATED
apps/web/lib/agents/agent-registry.ts:51,57  forbiddenActions applied to every agent
apps/web/app/api/ops/props-slate/route.ts:63  PROPS_SLATE_ENABLED === '1' -- and no cron entry exists for it
gaps.impact: Doctrine (B) is not prose; it is code. The prohibitions are real and they are inconsistent with a model that publishes: the props route is gated off with no cron, the content worker refuses everything, agent publishing does not compile, and CI blocks any publish-side write in the scanned paths. Meanwhile the Oct-18 board was published by a script OUTSIDE the guardrail's scan set -- which is how both can be true at once.
gaps.recommended_action: Reconcile the guardrail with the business model: give the publish surface a named boundary that draft-only.mjs allowlists, decide the props route's cron, and split PUBLISH out of FORBIDDEN_EXTERNAL_ACTIONS into a gated capability. Until then, the repo has two mutually exclusive publishing postures and no document says which is live.
